title: A Hundred Is Ten Tens
keyIdea: One hundred is ten tens. In place value, the hundreds digit counts groups of 100 — ten rods of ten make one hundred flat.
familyTip: Build 100 with ten ten-rods, then swap for one flat. Ask: 'Still 100 ones?' Try reading 130 as 1 hundred and 3 tens.

visual.caption: Hundred = ten tens — fair idea or myth? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: swapping 10 tens for 1 hundred keeps the total

lab.caption: Flagship lab: bundle 10 tens into a hundred, read 110, swap without changing total, build 100, compare flats vs tens, then challenge.

kid: A hundred is ten tens stuck together.
One tall ten-rod is 10. Ten of those rods make 100 — a hundred flat.
When you swap 10 tens for 1 hundred, you still have the same number of ones.
Read hundreds first, then tens: 1 hundred and 3 tens is 130.
adult: NC Y2 / CCSS 2.NBT.A.1: 100 is a bundle of ten tens; the hundreds place counts units of 100. Words: hundred, ten, flat, rod, regroup, place value.
Common mistakes: treating a hundred as ten ones; reading 1 hundred and 1 ten as 11; thinking regrouping changes the total; saying more pieces always means more value.
In the lab your child bundles 10 tens into a flat, reads 110, swaps tens for a hundred (total stays 100), builds 100, and sees 12 tens beat 1 hundred.

practice.hint: Ten rods of ten join into one hundred.
